items.title: Bill Dobbins interviewed by Monk Rowe, Rochester, New York, January 11, 2012
items.q: I think he wrote it around ’89, late 80s or early 90s — one is that the evolutionary process — and this is an idea also that was explored a little bit by Arthur Koestler, a really brilliant novelist and humanist and writer who was born in Budapest and grew up and was educated in England.

ctx.x: Nervous of silence. That’s another phenomenon also I think more of our time too because we’re surrounded with so much extraneous noise all the time. Because every time you go into a restaurant or a shopping mall or anywhere, some kind of music or noise is ubiquitous. And because of that, even the very idea that there is, or could be, an inner life, which is my real life — I mean that’s where the action is all the time, whether I’m looking at you or looking out the window here, or listening to a piece of music, or…

same thing. And in one of those books, I think it was the one on science, he was one of the first people to start using this term “holon” H-O-L-O-N which is the concept of how the universe is really put together, because since we’ve become aware that just as there is an infinity from the cell up to the whole cosmos, there is one in the other direction too, that the subatomic particles and on and on and on and on. So it goes to infinity both ways. But in that chain, each thing is both — each thing that has evolved…
